subject: SOC 2 reporting slice: mid-period system migration and log capture
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ava Stone <ava@acme-audit.com>, ClientCorp Security <security@clientcorp.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 reporting slice: mid-period system migration and log capture

Hi Ava / ClientCorp security team,

Quick one from the SOC 2 prep side — we’ve scheduled a platform migration that will move a subset of inference routing (legacy pool -> new autoscaling pool) at 02:00 UTC on 2026-09-18. Because of the migration timing and upstream billing/backup windows, part of the migration activity will land on different calendar days depending on timezone.

Two concrete asks:
1) For the Type II period that ends on 2026-09-30, will a migration that starts at 02:00 UTC on 2026-09-18 be considered inside the reporting period as of the point-in-time? In other words, do you prefer an explicit inclusive/exclusive timestamp for the period end or do you treat the period as inclusive by default?
2) If controls change during the migration (temporary fallback routing + config toggle), would a signed bridge-style statement describing the cutover window + a 48-hour log extract be considered sufficient evidence instead of rerunning additional control testing?

I’ve attached a brief timeline (system-migration-timeline.csv) and an index of the archived log buckets we propose to share (log-archive-index.txt). Draft bridge letter attached as well — this is an early draft for you to review.

Background/details: the migration involves a rolling update across three regions. Expected start: 2026-09-18 02:00:00 UTC; expected end of active change window: 2026-09-18 06:00:00 UTC. We will capture system and control logs continuously; the plan is to deliver redacted extracts for the full 48 hours around the window (2026-09-17 14:00:00 UTC through 2026-09-19 14:00:00 UTC) plus the signed bridge statement.

Can you confirm whether that approach aligns with what auditors typically accept for Type II coverage or if you want different timestamps or additional evidence (e.g., separation-of-duties checklist, change ticket export)?

Thanks — want to lock this down before we start the migration runbook.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov | Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

+1 on the 48-hour window. A couple of practical notes from ops/security:
- Please ensure all log exports specify UTC and include the bucket+path and object hashes (we should provide a short manifest).
- If we toggle a control (e.g., increase retry thresholds) include the change ticket ID and reviewer/approver.
- For separation-of-duties evidence, we can provide the runbook approvals and the change ticket audit trail — happy to attach if the auditor wants it.

If the auditor prefers a formal bridge letter template, suggest we share our draft and let them mark up.

Rishi
Principal Security Engineer

From: Ava Stone <ava@acme-audit.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: ClientCorp Security <security@clientcorp.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 reporting slice: mid-period system migration and log capture

Thanks for the clear summary, Olga — and thanks Rishi for the details. Short answers up front:

1) Reporting period inclusivity: auditors typically accept an explicit timestamped definition for the period (recommended), otherwise the period is interpreted as inclusive up to 23:59:59 on the stated end date in UTC unless your engagement letter specifies a different timezone. For mid-period events the key is to provide exact UTC timestamps for start/end of change windows and to indicate whether the control state during that window is equivalent to the operational state covered by the engagement.

2) Bridge statement vs additional testing: a signed bridge statement that describes the control changes, includes the exact UTC windows, and is accompanied by contemporaneous evidence (change ticket exports, runbook approvals, and the requested 48-hour log extracts with object hashes) is generally acceptable as supporting evidence. Whether additional testing is required depends on the materiality and nature of the control change; for a routing/config toggle that does not materially alter authentication/authorization controls, we usually accept a bridge statement + logs and no additional testing. If the change impacts segregation of duties or introduces a new third-party that handles secrets/keys, we will likely request expanded testing.

Action items for you:
- Please provide the log manifest (bucket path + object name + sha256) and a redacted sample event (one per log type) in UTC.
- Update the bridge-letter-draft.docx to include the signed approver name, role, and the exact UTC cutover window.
- Provide the change ticket export (Jira ID + history) for the migration.

If you want, I can mark up your draft bridge letter and return a version that the audit team will accept. For turnaround, aim to send artifacts by EOD 2026-09-17 so we can review ahead of our internal evidence checklist.

Regards,
Ava Stone, Senior Auditor
Acme Audit LLP

Requested timeline: please send by 2026-09-17 EOD to allow review before evidence cutoff.

Please let me know if the above is sufficient for the Type II evidence set or if you need us to expand the sample sizes / provide additional control artifacts. I can also accept Ava’s markup on the bridge letter and return a signed copy within 24 hours.

Thanks — will await confirmation so we can proceed with the migration runbook.

Best,
